newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo says strikes threaten production.
newsitem.headline: Volvo says strikes threaten production.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo said on Thursday it expected difficulties maintaining production next week if truckers' strikes in France and Denmark continue.

"I think we can keep production going today and on Friday. But we foresee great difficulties in the beginning of next week for our plants in Gent, Born and Torslanda," Volvo Car spokesman Ingmar Hesslefors told Reuters.

Hesslefors said the Gent, Belgium plant would be hit hardest because instrument panels used in production there are manufactured in France. There could also be a shortage of electrical cables, which are made in Spain but are shipped through France, he said.
"We are working intensively to find alternative transportation solutions, perhaps through other traffic routes like sea or by air," Hesslefors said.
The strike by Danish lorry drivers, which is not related to the industrial action by French truckers, would have less of an impact, Hesslefors said.
"There are possibilities to use ferries directly to Germany or over the North Sea," he said.
He declined to say how much a production stop would cost Volvo's car division.
"It's not possible to say. It depends on how much we can recover later," he said.
